authority: CEO Round 139: 'Replace the single portfolio score with SCIENTIFIC_AQ and DECISION_AQ. The global scheduler can then choose using a documented policy rather than hiding two distinct concepts inside one number.'
problem: Round 138's single portfolio score mixed scientific information gain with buyer impact and cost into one scalar. A commercially interesting experiment could outrank a scientifically decisive falsification test and distort the discovery engine.

SCIENTIFIC_AQ.definition: How much does this experiment change our belief about whether the mechanism is real?

inputs.EIG: Expected information gain about the hypothesis (entropy reduction)
inputs.hypothesis_discrimination: Probability that this experiment discriminates the highest-posterior hypothesis from alternatives
inputs.independence: Does this experiment use an independent source/solver/world? (0=internal, 1=external)
inputs.scientific_cost: Compute hours + installation friction + validation cost

SCIENTIFIC_AQ.what_it_measures: Scientific epistemic progress — can we trust the mechanism more after this experiment?
SCIENTIFIC_AQ.what_it_does_NOT_measure: Commercial viability, buyer willingness-to-pay, market size

DECISION_AQ.definition: How much does this experiment change the decision to continue/invest/sell/abandon?

inputs.P_decision_change: Probability that this experiment changes a go/no-go/invest/abandon decision
inputs.consequence: Economic/strategic consequence of the decision change (dollars, time, competitive position)
inputs.decision_cost: Cost of running the experiment (research hours, engagement effort)

DECISION_AQ.what_it_measures: Commercial/strategic decision progress — should we invest more in this candidate?
DECISION_AQ.what_it_does_NOT_measure: Whether the mechanism is physically real

scheduling_policy.rule: The scheduler records BOTH scores for every experiment. It then selects using a documented policy:
policy_options: SCIENTIFIC_FIRST: Always execute the highest SCIENTIFIC_AQ experiment first. DECISION_AQ breaks ties.
DECISION_FIRST: Always execute the highest DECISION_AQ experiment first. SCIENTIFIC_AQ breaks ties.
BALANCED: Execute the experiment with the highest product SCIENTIFIC_AQ × DECISION_AQ.
PORTFOLIO_BALANCED: Ensure that at least one scientific and one decision experiment are always in progress.
scheduling_policy.default_policy: SCIENTIFIC_FIRST — the discovery engine's primary purpose is finding truth, not maximizing commercial return. Scientific falsification takes priority. Decision-value experiments run in parallel or when scientific experiments are blocked.
scheduling_policy.rationale: Per Article I (evidence precedes assertion): scientific evidence must come before commercial claims. Per Article XXVIII (no silent semantic promotion): buyer-value assumptions cannot increase mechanism confidence.

C2_claim_level_prior_art.policy_note: High SCIENTIFIC (prior-art survival is a science gate) and high DECISION (affects IP strategy)

C5_actual_clotfoam.policy_note: Highest SCIENTIFIC per independence but high cost. BLOCKED on OpenFOAM.

C5_parameter_independence.policy_note: Low SCIENTIFIC (internal custom world, no independence) but high DECISION (cheap, fast). Under SCIENTIFIC_FIRST policy, this ranks LOW.

C1_reality_blocker_stride.policy_note: Highest EIG but REALITY-BLOCKED. Scheduler should not attempt to execute.

C3_buyer_value_chain.policy_note: Pure DECISION experiment. Under SCIENTIFIC_FIRST policy, runs only when scientific experiments are blocked.

calibration_requirement.rule: Do not permanently hard-code P(success) or P(decision_change) without calibration.

for_each_completed_experiment: Record: predicted_EIG, actual_epistemic_change, predicted_decision_impact, actual_decision_change, resource_cost, surprise
Update: if predicted > actual consistently for an experiment class, lower future predictions for that class
Learn: which experiment classes systematically outperform their forecasts
calibration_metrics: surprise_rate: fraction of experiments whose outcome was outside the predicted distribution

calibration_requirement.current_status: NOT YET CALIBRATED — all probabilities are model-assigned. The scheduler is a useful prioritization tool but not yet a learning system. Calibration begins when enough experiments have been completed to form a statistical baseline.
